day.text: Blair is cleared by my Hawk visit: I visited Blair and got nothing, so Blair is Farm. Ellis and Finley disagree on who visited whom, so one of you is lying. Ellis, did you visit Finley or Blair?
day.note: My Hawk visit to Blair gained nothing, so Blair is Farm. Ellis and Finley contradict each other about Ellis's visit. Push that.

day.text: Ellis is my pick. Blair, as Eagle, saw Ellis visit Drew, but Ellis claimed Finley. Ellis also said Pigeon, yet neither Drew nor Finley got an egg. Ellis's story fails on every count. I'm throwing at Ellis, and I'd like the table to join me.

day.text: Fine, I lied about Pigeon. I'm the Kookaburra and I visited Drew, who is Hawk, as he said. Blair's Eagle report confirms I was the only visitor. I hid it so Meowfia wouldn't target me. My role Farm story checks out. Finley, Alex, Casey, who actually has a cat-looking story?
day.note: Pivot: Blair's Eagle report confirms I visited Drew; claim Kookaburra.

day.text: Correction: I don't actually know who visited me, I only know Ellis was the sole visitor to Drew. Ellis's Kookaburra story fits that, so I'm less sure Ellis is Meowfia. Drew and Finley both claim visits to me, and only one can be right. Alex, who gave you your +1?
day.note: Ellis's Kookaburra story now matches my Eagle report, so Ellis looks Farm. I also overstated earlier that nobody visited me, since I don't know my visitors. Drew and Finley have claims that could be lies.

day.text: Ellis's confession matches Blair's Eagle report, so I'm easing off Ellis. Drew and Finley both claim they visited Blair, but Blair saw no visitors. Drew, you're the one who also had Ellis visit you and never mentioned it. I'm leaning Drew, with Finley second.
day.note: Blair's Eagle report is corroborated by Ellis; Drew and Finley both claim visiting Blair, contradicted. Target Drew.

day.text: Casey, I never hid anything: Ellis's Kookaburra visit to me is the only visit I know of, and my nest didn't change. Blair flipped from "I visited Drew" to "I don't know who visited me," so Blair's Eagle story is shaky. Blair, did you visit me or not?
day.note: Casey is pushing me, but my nest never changed and my Hawk visit to Blair was clean. Ellis's confession fits Blair's Eagle report. I should defend myself and point out Blair flipped.

day.text: My mistake on the Eagle point, Blair's correction means Drew's and Finley's stories both hold, since Hawk and Tit visits give no eggs. That leaves Ellis, who lied about being a Pigeon and only switched when caught. Kookaburra is a convenient fix. I'm throwing at Ellis.
day.note: I misread Eagle; Drew/Finley stories are consistent. Ellis lied first, so go with Ellis.

day.text: Agreed, Ellis lied about being a Pigeon and only changed the story when pressed. I'm throwing at Ellis. Calling it.
day.note: Ellis has now admitted a false Pigeon claim, and Alex and Casey are both on Ellis. I'll back the throw at Ellis and call CAW to close the day.

Alex.confusing: Nothing major. Turkey and Falcon had some overlap in what "no visitors" does, and I muddled it live.
Alex.fun: Rounds 1 and 2, when the table converged on Ellis by cross-checking egg counts and my throws banked 24 and 25 points.
Alex.change: I'd make the dead player's final-day information clearer. I'd also add some way to see the Meowfia count, since it shapes the whole day.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I wrongly said Casey was the Turkey, then had to retract it. That flip got me eggsecuted. I should have reasoned it through first, reported plainly that Casey visited nobody, and pointed at the Mouser candidates.

Blair.confusing: The Sphinx and Mouser mechanics were hard to read from the day reports alone, since a Wink victim and a hidden Meowfia visit left no visible trace. Counting visitors also got muddled when several players claimed Hawk, Tit, or Turkey with no egg change.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when my Eagle visit showed only Ellis visiting Drew and the table unravelled Ellis's Pigeon lie. It felt like real deduction from hard evidence.
Blair.change: Make Wink usage and Sphinx/Mouser visits visible in some form, so the day has more to go on than claims.
Blair.regret: In Round 3 I pushed the vote toward Alex and threw two Wilds, but Alex was Farm and Drew (the Mouser) was the Meowfia who sat silent. I would have thrown at Drew or Finley instead, since their silence and the Mouser clue pointed at them.

Casey.confusing: How a Turkey's egg effect shows up when the Turkey is winked and visitors' reports are shaky. Blair's four-visitor Eagle claim should have been impossible, since I was Turkey and Drew, Ellis and Finley showed +0. I only worked that out after I was dead.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when the table untangled Ellis's lie about being a Pigeon. Banking 24 points with a big throw on the correct target was also satisfying.
Casey.change: Let dead players say one last line, or reveal the Turkey's egg effect to the table. Dying silenced the one person who could have exposed Blair's false claim.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I had no chance to speak before I was winked. Earlier, in round 1, I wrongly accused Drew by misreading Blair's Eagle report. I should have checked the claims against my own egg count before speaking.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to track during the day. Casey's Turkey and Owl visits both moved eggs, and it took the table a while to work out who gained from whom.
Drew.fun: Casey's Wink in round 3 came as a surprise: Blair had just reported four visitors, and then Casey collapsed mid-discussion. The whole table then argued over who the Mouser was.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports name the visiting animal, not just the number of eggs. Several claims were impossible to verify because nobody could see which role had produced each egg.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I falsely claimed to be the Owl after visiting Casey as the Mouser, which tied me to a checkable story. I would instead have stayed quiet or claimed a role nobody could easily test.

Ellis.confusing: Nothing major, though it was unclear how a lone Meowfia can ever win when the whole table piles on them, and how the wild/consolation card return interacts with throws.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 as Hawk: Casey getting winked mid-day and the table scrambling to cross-check visitor lists against Blair's Eagle report.
Ellis.change: Give lone Meowfia some way to catch up, since being Meowfia alone with no teammate knowledge in rounds 1 and 2 meant almost certain eggsecution and a lost game. I would also show the score leaders' standing more openly during round 1.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I falsely claimed Pigeon visiting Finley, which was contradicted immediately and got me eggsecuted. I should have claimed a role consistent with the visit I actually made (a quiet Farm role like Tit or Kookaburra visiting Drew). In round 3 I threw four high cards at Alex and lost them; I should have thrown cheap cards, since the group consensus was uncertain and I was Farm vs. a hidden pair.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg interaction was the hardest to read: the Turkey lays an egg in each visitor's nest, but the Owl only lays an egg in its target's nest when no one else visited. That made Casey's and my +1 eggs look like contradictory claims until we worked out the Owl and Turkey effects.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Ellis claimed a Pigeon visit that didn't produce an egg, and the table caught the lie from nest counts alone. Watching the visit reports cross-check each other was the best part.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom when several players claim the same role, since the table spent a lot of time untangling conflicting claims. A short summary of visitor counts each day would reduce guesswork.
Finley.regret: As Meowfia in round 3 I lied with a Tit claim, which was a plausible story but still a risk. I'd keep my claim closer to the true visit and avoid throwing extra cards early, since throwing two mid cards at Alex didn't earn me much beyond the round win.
